content.title: About
content.content: Caesar dressing fat free is a classic Caesar sauce made without added plant or dairy fats. It retains the characteristic flavor of Parmesan, garlic, anchovies and lemon juice, but has dramatically reduced calories and zero fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original Caesar sauce was created in the 1920s at Caesar's restaurant in Tijuana, Mexico.
Its iconic taste comes from the combination of anchovies, Parmesan cheese and egg yolk rather than oil.
Fat‑free versions often use yogurt or low‑fat kefir as the base.
Lemon juice and Worcestershire sauce give the sauce its distinctive tang and aroma.
Caesar dressing is commonly served with chicken, shrimp or vegetarian alternatives.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: The absence of fat lowers the energy density, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Egg yolk and Parmesan provide a modest amount of high‑quality protein.

items.title: Provides calcium
items.content: Parmesan adds calcium, which supports bone health.

items.title: Contains probiotics (when yogurt is used)
items.content: Low‑fat yogurt can contribute beneficial bacteria for gut health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: No added plant or dairy fats makes the dressing suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Parmesan may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Worcestershire sauce and anchovies can increase salt levels, which should be considered by people with hypertension.

items.title: Anchovies
items.content: Some individuals are sensitive to fish or seafood.

items.title: Raw eggs
items.content: Traditional recipes use raw egg yolks, posing a salmonella risk; fat‑free versions often use pasteurized eggs.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Fat‑free Caesar dressing is perfect for dressing salads (especially classic Caesar), as a marinade for chicken or fish, and as a dip for vegetable sticks. It can also be added to sandwiches or used in other sauces as a lower‑calorie alternative.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dressing in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Once opened, it is typically good for 5‑7 days. Discard if you notice off‑smell, taste changes, or mold.
